new_statements.rule_in_words: Korowai word stress is lexical: its position cannot be predicted from the shape of the word and it distinguishes minimal pairs (dámo 'say' vs damó 'close', láilo 'be broken' vs laílo 'ask'); stressed vowels are lengthened and unstressed non-final vowels reduce. De Vries 2020 (sec. 2.4.3) recharacterises the same system as 'Word stress is a contrastive pitch accent.'
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing on secondary stress in any accessible text (the vocabulary marks only 'main word stress').
new_statements.exceptions: Authors themselves are uncertain of stress placement for some vocabulary items (left unmarked); in compound nouns stress is likewise unpredictable; in perfect verb forms the main stress is on the verb stem, and stem-final vowels reduce when that stress is not on the stem's last syllable (snippets from pp. c. 88-99).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress on citation forms; stress is not written in the practical (Indonesian-based) orthography and is marked only in ch. 2 (acute accent) and in the vocabularies (underlining). Access caveat: the sentence was read only as machine-served verbatim snippets (Google Books volumes feed), corroborated by four independent fragments (1997 p.60, 1997 compounds remark, the WORD 2002 review, the 1998 Bird's Head volume) and by de Vries 2020; the full page was not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: nort3250 'North Korowai' is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for ISO 639-3 [krg], retired 2008-01-14 and merged into Korowai [khe] (Glottolog koro1312) on SIL evidence of ~90% lexical similarity and mutual intelligibility ('pronunciation is a bit different', CR 2007-222). No separate description of a northern variety exists. The quoted statement is van Enk & de Vries's description of Korowai [khe/koro1312] as a whole, based (as far as I understand the book's framing, not verified on an opened page) on van Enk's mission-era data from the Yaniruma/Manggél area at the southern edge of Korowai territory. The only material from the northern (Becking River) area is Hughes 2009's stress-marked 239-item wordlist from Abiowage, which shows stress on varying syllables but carries no analysis. Any catalog entry should be filed under koro1312, with nort3250 pointing to it.

sources.note: No statement. Sociolinguistic survey (Oct-Nov 2000); pp.10-11: 'The language name might be Korowai or North Korowai, if there is a significant difference.' Appendix V gives a 239-item IPA wordlist 'Korowai / Abiowage' (Becking River, northern Korowai area) with primary-stress marks on varying syllables (e.g. ʔɑ biˈɑːn 'head', ˈʔɯlmɔːm 'hit', kimɑːˈβoːn 'go', ʔæˈwuiβ 'language') -- raw data only.
